"Or you just remember the good nights," she said.
"Fine. Let's test it." For the next Friday he put up six posters and sent no messages. Ishita stood at the terrace door with a counter. Twenty-six came.
Week two. No posters at all, only one message in each class chat group, same time of day, same kind of sky forecast. Ishita counted again. Eleven.
Week three. Mohit wrote on the club notebook: posters 26, messages 11. "Two weeks isn't proof," he said. "But I'm keeping the posters, and we'll count again next month."
Ishita smiled. "At least now it's not just a feeling."
